notes: The FY 2026-27 adopted budget was not posted on the county website when checked. Only the FY 2026-27 proposed budget ($14.261 billion in total, $9.022 billion operating) was posted. This page uses the FY 2025-26 adopted budget instead.
The table is in thousands of dollars. Figures here are multiplied by 1,000.

This is the operating budget of $8.576 billion. The county also adopted a multi-year capital plan, and its total adopted budget of $13.233 billion also counts capital spending. Capital spending is not in this table.
The county groups departments into strategic areas (Public Safety, Transportation and Mobility, and so on). They are shown here as groups.

The enterprise departments are kept because the county counts them in its operating total: Aviation ($775 million), Water and Sewer ($861 million), Solid Waste Management ($445 million), Seaport ($177 million) and Transportation and Public Works ($834 million in Transportation and Mobility plus $71 million in Neighborhood and Infrastructure).
The county includes Jackson Health System ($349 million), the Library, and the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office and other constitutional offices in the same total.
Departments with $0 in FY 2025-26 are left out (for example Juvenile Services and the Tax Collector, which the county shows with prior-year funding only).

Departments pay each other for services. The county lists these Interagency Transfers ($925.7 million) as a separate line and subtracts them in its Grand Total so the same dollars are not counted twice. That line is shown here as a negative group.

notes: This is the budget the Board of Supervisors adopted on June 22, 2026. The Board later approved a Supplemental Budget in September 2026 ($54.2 billion on the county's "operating" basis); that later version is not broken out by department in the files the county posted, so it is not used here.

The county's own chart pages use a smaller "operating budget" figure ($50.3 billion at adoption). This page uses the larger "financing uses" total of $56.5 billion that the resolution prints, because that is the table that lists every fund. The two totals are measured differently, and this document does not reconcile them.

The General Fund line lists each budget unit as the resolution prints it. Some departments are split into several units; for example the Sheriff has separate units for custody, patrol, courts and more. Names that start with CP are capital project units inside the General Fund. Other prefixes (CFCI, PSS, DCFS, EP, PFU, ENT SUB) are the county's own unit labels and are kept as printed.
Budget-unit amounts are net of transfers between units (intrafund transfers). The General Fund line also has a separate amount the county sets aside for contingencies.
The other funds are shown as one line each by fund type. The resolution lists each individual fund on pages 9 to 12.
Capital projects are listed in a separate section of the resolution (a different table). They are not added to this total.

notes: The county groups its departments into six portfolios. They are shown here as groups. The group totals are from the portfolio table on page 46. Each department amount is the FY 2026/27 budget printed on that department's own page, so each department links to its page.

The Executive Office portfolio group includes Debt Service ($105.0 million), the County Capital Improvement Program ($53.7 million) and Capital Finance Administration ($49.8 million). Their amounts are the Total Uses lines in the budget tables on the pages linked.

Amounts are net of Intrafund Transfers, which the county subtracts inside each portfolio. Because of this, Countywide Cost Allocation Plan/Other shows as a negative number (a credit of $16.2 million).

The county reports a total of $10.4 billion in appropriations across all funds, up 3.7% ($370.7 million) from the FY 2025/26 adopted budget.
